Engines of pima()

Source: R/engines.R
pima_flipscores.Rd

The engine is the test used by pima() to test the coefficients of all the models jointly. pima_flipscores() and pima_multcomp() create an engine with its own arguments, passed to the engine argument of pima(). engine = "flipscores" and engine = "multcomp" use the engines with their default arguments.

Usage

pima_flipscores(n_flips = 5000, ...)

pima_multcomp(algorithm = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'pima_engine'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

n_flips

number of sign flips.

...

further arguments of flipscores::flipscores(), e.g. score_type. The arguments set by pima() (formula, data, tested_coeffs, id, seed) cannot be given.

algorithm

algorithm for the multivariate normal probabilities of the adjusted p-values, e.g. mvtnorm::GenzBretz(maxpts = 1e6, abseps = 1e-6) for more precise (and slower) results. If NULL (default), the default of multcomp.

x

an engine.

Value

An object of class pima_engine: a list with the name of the engine and its args.

Details

The arguments shared by the engines (tested_coeffs, method, tail, extra, id, seed) are arguments of pima(). See the Engines section of pima() for the tests.

See also

Other PIMA inference: pima(), pima-method, pima_tree()

Examples

mods <- list(
  a = glm(Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length, data = iris),
  b = glm(Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Species, data = iris)
)
pima(mods, tested_coeffs = "Sepal.Length", seed = 1,
     engine = pima_flipscores(n_flips = 500, score_type = "basic"))
#> 
#> == Multiverse analysis with 2 scenarios ==
#> 
#>   model                              formula   family     link   Intercept
#> 1     a           Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length gaussian identity (Intercept)
#> 2     b Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Species gaussian identity (Intercept)
#>   Sepal.Length  Species
#> 1 Sepal.Length excluded
#> 2 Sepal.Length  Species
#> 

pima_flipscores(n_flips = 500)
#> <pima engine: flipscores>
#>   n_flips: 500
pima_multcomp()
#> <pima engine: multcomp>
#>   algorithm: NULL
